sections.title: Basic Concept of Idioms and Phrases
sections.content: Idioms and phrases are groups of words whose meanings are different from the literal meanings of the individual words. To understand them correctly, it is necessary to understand the entire expression or sentence. In competitive exams, questions often ask for the correct meaning of an idiom or its meaning within a sentence.

sections.title: Direct Meaning of Idioms
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire idiom as a single unit instead of interpreting each word separately. Step 2: Remember its commonly accepted meaning. Step 3: Choose the option that best matches that meaning. Example: 'Break the ice' means to start a conversation.

sections.title: Contextual Meaning in Sentence
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire sentence carefully. Step 2: Observe the situation expressed by the idiom. Step 3: Select the meaning that fits the context. Example: 'He finally broke the ice and started the conversation.' Here it means starting a conversation.

sections.title: Commonly Used Idioms
sections.content: Some idioms frequently appear in competitive exams such as: 'A piece of cake' (very easy), 'Hit the nail on the head' (to say something exactly right), 'Under the weather' (to feel ill).

sections.title: Understanding Context
sections.content: Sometimes the meaning of an idiom becomes clear from the context of the sentence. Therefore, it is important to read the entire sentence rather than focusing only on the idiom.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Taking the literal meaning of the words in an idiom. 2. Ignoring the context of the sentence. 3. Confusing idioms that look or sound similar.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: The meaning of idioms cannot be understood from the individual words alone. Remembering the standard meanings and understanding the context of the sentence helps in selecting the correct answer.

tricks.title: Whole Phrase Rule
tricks.explanation: Understand the idiom as a complete phrase with a fixed meaning.
tricks.example: A piece of cake = a very easy task.

tricks.title: Context Reading Trick
tricks.explanation: Read the entire sentence to understand the meaning of the idiom.
tricks.example: The exam was a piece of cake for her. (Meaning: very easy).

tricks.title: Common Idiom Memory
tricks.explanation: Memorize idioms that frequently appear in exams.
tricks.example: Hit the nail on the head = to say something exactly right.

tricks.title: Opposite Situation Trick
tricks.explanation: Use the situation in the sentence to identify whether the idiom expresses a positive or negative idea.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: Remove options that clearly do not match the meaning to find the correct answer quickly.
tricks.example: If someone 'spills the beans', it means revealing a secret.

tricks.title: Short Story Trick
tricks.explanation: Associate the idiom with a short example or story to remember it easily.
tricks.example: Break the ice = starting a conversation for the first time.

tricks.title: Emotion Clue Trick
tricks.explanation: Identify the emotion or situation associated with the idiom.
tricks.example: In hot water = being in trouble.

tricks.title: Usage Practice Trick
tricks.explanation: Practice using the idiom in sentences to remember it better.
tricks.example: After the mistake, he was in hot water with his boss.
